summary: An interactive 3D educational space exploration game designed to make space science and spacecraft engineering more accessible and engaging for everyone. Instead of simply reading about spacecraft, players learn through hands-on experiences. They begin in a spacecraft workshop, where they assemble their own vehicle using different components, including command pods, instrument packages, fuel tanks, and engines. Each component affects the spacecraft's mass, thrust, fuel capacity, and overall flight performance. Once their spacecraft is ready, players can launch it into a simulated flight, manage engine throttle, monitor their vehicle's performance, and experience the consequences of their engineering decisions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

A.T.L.A.S is a browser-native, 3D interactive solar system explorer and space mission engineering platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It operates across two seamless modes:

  • Let’s Explore: Users navigate an interactive 3D solar system powered by real Keplerian orbital physics, inspect 5-layer planetary science data (including Earth and target moons/planets), and scrub through a cosmic history timeline.
  • Play Game: Solo explorers or 4-player specialist crews customize astronaut avatars, design modular spacecraft in a collapsible CAD drawer, pass a NASA-style Go/No-Go readiness poll, and execute a 5-phase mission lifecycle—from 3D orbital ascent to procedural planetary surface landing.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Zero-Barrier Access: Requires zero installation or high-end workstations, running directly in modern web browsers with responsive accessibility layers.
  • Democratizing Aerospace Education: Contextual tooltips translate dense orbital mechanics and spacecraft engineering terminology for beginners, turning passive observation into hands-on scientific problem-solving.
  • Collaborative STEM Engagement: Role-based multiplayer lobbies mirror real mission control teamwork, inspiring students and space enthusiasts to learn astrophysics through cooperative mission planning.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages & Markup: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+ modular architecture across 37 specialized core, engine, shader, and game modules), and GLSL (OpenGL Shading Language).
  • Graphics & Audio Engines: Custom WebGL planetary rendering library with a lazy GPU texture baker for procedural terrains, plus a Web Audio API sound synthesis engine for real-time spacecraft telemetry audio.
  • Styling & Tooling: Tailwind CSS, Node.js syntax verification scripts (check-syntax.mjs), and VS Code.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

  • Creative Synthesis: Rather than separating data visualization from gameplay, ATLAS unifies scientific planetary telemetry, procedural surface shaders, and an interactive 10-chapter AI guide bot (ATLAS Instructor) inside a single tactile mission-control interface.
    • Beginner Onboarding vs. Realism: Balancing accurate Keplerian orbital calculations and spacecraft propulsion trade-offs with simplified dashboard modes and plain-language tooltips.
    • Performance: Implementing lazy GPU texture baking so complex planetary surfaces load smoothly across standard consumer hardware.
    • Inclusivity: Designing both solo character studios and 4-player crew synchronization to accommodate different learning and play styles.
